findings.english_quote: looked into the furnace and spoke of a fourth
findings.issue: τέταρτον is the object of ἐνιδών: the narrator says that Nebuchadnezzar perceived a fourth person in the furnace. The draft instead describes looking into the furnace and attaches the fourth person to speaking. Although the following quotation reports his seeing, it does not preserve this narrated construction accurately.
findings.suggested_revision: Replace this wording with “saw a fourth in the furnace and said,” followed by the existing quotation. Review the revised sentence afresh.

findings.source_quote: δηλονότι ὡς ἐμοῦ καταγνωσθέντος καὶ ἐμοῦ ἀδοκίμου ὄντος
findings.english_quote: as though I had clearly been condemned and were unapproved.
findings.issue: The placement of “clearly” changes the scope of δηλονότι. Here it introduces an explanation of the alleged grounds for withholding belief; the draft embeds it within the supposed condemnation, making that condemnation itself clear.
findings.suggested_revision: Use an explanatory construction such as “—that is, as though I had been condemned and were unapproved.” Review the replacement in its complete sentence.

findings.english_quote: show direct perception to be more evident than an apparition
findings.issue: ἐνάργειαν and ἐναργεστέραν visibly repeat the same lexical root, whereas “direct perception” and “more evident” conceal that pattern. The note incorrectly says that the evidence/evident wording has been retained. It also assumes that ὀπτασίας is a comparative genitive without disclosing the alternative attachment to ἐνάργειαν, “the vividness/evidence of an apparition.” The comparative interpretation is defensible, but its rationale and material alternative need to be recorded.
findings.suggested_revision: Compare the current wording explicitly with a source-transparent candidate such as “show evidence more evident than an apparition.” Revise the main wording to preserve the lexical repetition, and explain in a note why ὀπτασίας is taken with the comparative rather than possessively with ἐνάργειαν. Preserve the alternative without presenting it as a correction to the printed Greek. Any replacement requires fresh review.

findings.source_quote: σὺ δὲ ὡς ἠθέλησας εἶπες, οὐχ ἔδειξας.
findings.english_quote: But you said what you wished; you did not demonstrate it.
findings.issue: ὡς describes how Peter spoke, not an object specifying what he said. The draft shifts the criticism from speaking as he wished to saying whatever content he wished.
findings.suggested_revision: Use “But you spoke as you wished; you did not demonstrate it.” Review this proposed wording in context.

findings.source_quote: καὶ τὸν σὸν δὲ διδάσκαλον τὰ αὐτά μοι εἰρηκέναι
findings.english_quote: I will also show that your teacher said the same things as I
findings.issue: The draft defensibly takes μοι as a dative of comparison associated with τὰ αὐτά. However, μοι can also be the recipient of εἰρηκέναι: “your teacher said the same things to me.” That alternative materially changes whether Simon alleges agreement with his position or teaching addressed to him, and it is not disclosed.
findings.suggested_revision: The existing main interpretation may be retained provisionally, but add a source-quoted note preserving “your teacher said the same things to me” and explaining why comparison with Simon’s asserted position is preferred in context. This is an attachment ambiguity, not evidence of source corruption; review the revised passage and note afresh.
